title: Pinned model stability guarantees and onboarding checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a minimal, testable stability contract for pinned model versions so customers who pin a model version (e.g., model@v1.5) get strong guarantees about prompt/response shape, parameter semantics, and performance profiles. This ticket codifies the contract, the onboarding checklist for new models, the CI gating tests, and the publishing workflow for performance metadata.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: formalizing behavior guarantees for prompt format (system/user/message role semantics), structured output JSON schemas, stable parameter semantics (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, function/tool call protocol), tokenization edge-case behavior for prefix caching, documented error codes and retry semantics, and performance profile publishing (p50/p95 latency, throughput for standard batch sizes, memory/kv-cache footprints).
- Out of scope: model training changes, internal kernel-level optimizations. This ticket focuses on onboarding and guarantees for served artifacts.

Contract surface (high level):
1) Prompt/Message semantics: system/user/assistant role semantics must be preserved; legacy single-string prompts must continue to be accepted but treated as a single user message. Any change to role interpretation requires a documented behavioral migration note and an opt-in flag.
2) Structured output: when a model is published with a structured-output schema, the schema version and examples must be bundled with the model artifact. The runtime will validate top-level JSON shape for required fields and return a defined error type (MODEL_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION) if validation fails.
3) Parameter semantics: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop tokens, and presence penalties must map to the previously published semantics; any change to sampling implementation requires a backward-compat alias mapping for at least two minor versions or a deprecation window documented in the model profile.
4) Tokenization and KV cache: changes that alter token boundaries for identical byte sequences are forbidden for pinned versions. If tokenization changes are necessary, a new pinned minor must be published and runtime will offer automatic cached-prefix translation where possible.
5) Error and edge-case behaviors: define canonical error codes for user-visible failures (RATE_LIMITED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, MODEL_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION, INTERNAL_INFERENCE_ERROR, MODEL_DEGRADATION_DETECTED). The contract specifies retry/backoff recommendations in the model profile.
6) Performance profile guarantees: each pinned release must include measured latency percentiles (p50, p95) under defined request shapes and batch sizes, throughput (tokens/sec), and memory footprint. Published profiles should include measurement harness details and raw benchmark artifact links.

Onboarding checklist for a new pinned model version (must be completed before marking the release as pinned):
- Model artifact uploaded and checksum verified.
- Schema doc: prompt examples, accepted parameter set, and structured-output schema (if any) committed to models.redwood.com/docs repo.
- Behavioral tests: 100+ deterministic prompt tests covering role semantics, stop token handling, function calling, and at least 20 structured-output validation cases.
- Performance tests: benchmark runs for single-request latency (sequences 32/128/512), sustained throughput with typical batch sizes, and cold-start measurements. Attach raw results.
- Regression harness: diff against previous pinned minor with flagged behavioral regressions to be triaged.
- Security review: KMS usage, key access boundaries, and data retention notes.
- Rollout plan: canary percentage schedule, fallback variant mapping, and automatic rollback triggers.

CI gating and tests:
- Add model-specific test suite to the onboarding CI job. Required checks: unit-style determinism tests, structured-output schema validation, and a lightweight perf smoke test.
- A separate nightly regression job compares new pinned candidate to previous pinned minor on a fixed prompt corpus; any semantic diffs above thresholds create a blocking failure.

Rollout, monitoring, and rollback rules:
- Default rollout: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over configurable window (default 48h) with human in the loop for any semantic diff or customer-facing error.
- Alerting: model degradation (increase in schema violations, hallucination rate on eval prompts, or error rate) triggers a P1 incident and automatic rollback to previous pinned minor if thresholds exceeded for 10 minutes.
- Observability: each pinned model must publish a dashboard tile with request volume, p95 latency, error rates, schema violation counts, and customer-level impacts.

Publishing performance profiles and model metadata:
- Profiles must live alongside the model in the model catalog and include: measurement harness version, hardware used, sequence lengths, batch sizes, and raw logs link.
- Profiles are immutable for a pinned version; corrections require a new minor pinned release.

Trade-offs and decisions recorded so far:
- We accept a modest increase in onboarding friction (extra tests and artifacts) to obtain strong guarantees for customers who pin.
- We will not automatically translate or re-tokenize customer cached prefixes for major model architecture changes; these require explicit migration guidance or an opt-in translation service.
- Performance guarantees will be soft (measured in our harness) and accompanied by SLOs only for Dedicated/Enterprise tiers. Hosted users get the published profiles but not hard SLO credits unless on Dedicated.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define the exact threshold for semantic-diff gating in nightly regression (initial proposal: >2% token-level divergence on canonical prompts or >5% structured-field mismatch).
- Finalize the list of canonical prompts for nightly regression and ensure dataset licensing for public examples.
- Implement runtime flagging for role-interpretation changes so older pinned versions are unaffected.
